mainTopic: The week before מתן תורה: the timelines of רבי יוסי and the רבנן, the three things משה did on his own with ה׳'s approval, and the challenges from the 'third' and 'sixth' day ברייתות
overview: This amud finishes רבי יוסי's day-by-day timeline of the week before מתן תורה, then gives the רבנן's timeline, which runs one day later. The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי from the פסוק "היום ומחר", which implies only two days of separation. It answers that משה added a third day on his own. A ברייתא lists three things משה did on his own that ה׳ agreed with: adding a day, separating from his wife, and breaking the לוחות. For each one, the גמרא explains משה's reasoning and gives the proof that ה׳ approved. The גמרא then returns to the date dispute. רבי יוסי is defended again with משה's extra day, and ברייתות that fit only רבי יוסי's calendar are shown to follow him, so they do not bind the רבנן. Along the way, a ברייתא explains that the 'third' day was the day of הגבלה, and רבי and others explain the words וישב and ויגד. The amud ends as רבא begins to explain what the 'sixth' day means according to the רבנן, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רבי יוסי's timeline: boundaries on the third day, separation on the fourth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי's timeline ends: on Tuesday the מצוה of הגבלה was given, and on Wednesday the people began פרישה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the third day of the week, ה׳ told them the מצוה of setting boundaries around the mountain. On the fourth day, they separated from their wives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the timeline of רבי יוסי, which began on the previous amud. He says the boundaries were set on Tuesday and husbands and wives separated on Wednesday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that ראש חודש סיון fell on Sunday. So separation started on Wednesday, which means three days of separation (Wednesday, Thursday, Friday) before the Torah was given on שבת. Keep this number, three days, in mind, because it will be challenged in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: On the third day of the week (Tuesday)
The command to set boundaries around הר סיני
Separation of husbands from wives before מתן תורה
The תנא whose timeline is being finished here

phrases.english: On the third day of the week, He told them the מצוה of setting boundaries;
on the fourth day, they performed separation.
phrases.notes: According to רבי יוסי, this gives three days of separation before שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוסי's timeline, which began earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי: הגבלה was on Tuesday and פרישה began on Wednesday, giving three days of separation.

steps.title: The רבנן's timeline is shifted one day later
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold ראש חודש was on Monday, so every event is one day later and separation begins on Thursday.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: ראש חודש was set on Monday. On Monday ה׳ said nothing to them because they were tired from the trip. On Tuesday He told them "And you shall be to Me...". On Wednesday He gave the מצוה of setting boundaries. On Thursday they separated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the רבנן's version of the week. Their timeline is the same sequence as רבי יוסי's, but every event happens one day later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because ראש חודש was Monday, separation only started on Thursday. That gives just two days of separation (Thursday and Friday). This fits neatly with the פסוק "היום ומחר" (today and tomorrow), which is why the coming challenge is aimed at רבי יוסי and not at the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who disagree with רבי יוסי
The new month (ראש חודש) was established
The weariness of the journey
"And you shall be to Me" — the message of being a holy nation (שמות יט:ו)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
on the second day of the week the New Moon was established,

phrases.aramaic: בִּתְרֵי בְּשַׁבָּא לָא אֲמַר לְהוּ וְלָא מִידֵּי
phrases.english: on the second day of the week He did not say anything to them
because of the weariness of the journey;
on the third day He said to them: "And you shall be to Me";
on the fourth day He told them the מצוה of setting boundaries;
on the fifth day they performed separation.
phrases.notes: This gives two days of separation: Thursday and Friday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing timeline to רבי יוסי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן: ראש חודש was Monday and separation began Thursday, giving two days of separation.

steps.title: The verse says only "today and tomorrow" — a problem for רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "וקדשתם היום ומחר" implies only two days of separation, which contradicts רבי יוסי's three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: the פסוק says "Sanctify them today and tomorrow." That is difficult for רבי יוסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי from a פסוק‎. ה׳ told משה to sanctify the people "today and tomorrow", which sounds like only two days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's timeline produced three days of separation, but the פסוק names only two. The רבנן's two-day timeline matches the פסוק perfectly, so only רבי יוסי has a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (usually from a source)
"And sanctify them today and tomorrow" (שמות יט:י)
It is difficult; a challenge

phrases.english: They raised an objection: "And sanctify them today and tomorrow",
this is difficult for Rabbi Yosei!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a פסוק that fits the רבנן to attack רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's three days of separation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק explicitly mentions only two days ("today and tomorrow"), but רבי יוסי counts three.

steps.title: משה added one day on his own
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that ה׳ commanded two days, but משה added a third day based on his own understanding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי can tell you: משה added one day on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוסי. The פסוק records ה׳'s command of two days, but משה himself added a third day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק and רבי יוסי are no longer in conflict. The פסוק describes what ה׳ said, and רבי יוסי describes what actually happened after משה extended it. A source for this idea comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you — introduces a defense of someone's view
On his own understanding or initiative
He added

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei could say to you:
Moses added one day on his own initiative.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between the original command and the actual practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק's two days must be the total number of days of separation.
steps.terutzMaskana: ה׳ commanded two days, and משה added a third, so in practice there were three.

steps.title: A ברייתא: three things משה did on his own
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the answer: משה did three things on his own and ה׳ agreed. He added a day, he separated from his wife, and he broke the לוחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: משה did three things on his own, and ה׳ agreed with him. He added one day on his own, he separated from his wife, and he broke the לוחות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the idea of משה adding a day is an established tradition. The ברייתא lists three things משה did on his own that ה׳ approved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns the answer in step 4 from a guess into a sourced tradition. It also sets up the rest of this passage, where the גמרא goes through each item and asks what משה's reasoning was and how we know ה׳ agreed.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
And ה׳ agreed with him
And he separated from his wife (permanently)
And he broke the tablets

steps.whatToRemember: Three things משה did on his own with ה׳'s approval: (1) he added a day of separation before מתן תורה, (2) he separated from his wife, (3) he broke the לוחות.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים עָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה מִדַּעְתּוֹ,
phrases.english: As it was taught: Moses did three things on his own initiative,
and the Holy One, Blessed be He, agreed with him.
He added one day on his own initiative,
and he separated from his wife,
and he broke the tablets.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים עָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה מִדַּעְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides a source for the תירוץ.
steps.raayaObject: That משה added one day on his own
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing three things משה did on his own

steps.title: What was משה's reasoning for adding a day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which פסוק or reasoning led משה to add a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: He added one day on his own — what did he interpret?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins going through the ברייתא's list. It asks what reasoning led משה to add the extra day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה did not act at random; he must have learned it from ה׳'s words. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What did he expound or interpret?

phrases.aramaic: הוֹסִיף יוֹם אֶחָד מִדַּעְתּוֹ, מַאי דְּרַשׁ?
phrases.english: He added one day on his own initiative — what did he interpret?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the first item of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reasoning behind משה adding a day

steps.title: "Today is like tomorrow": each day needs its night
steps.stepSummary: משה reasoned that "today" must be like "tomorrow", a full day including the night before it. Since that night had already passed, he needed two full days after the current one.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Today and tomorrow" means today must be like tomorrow. Just as tomorrow includes its night, so too today must include its night. But the night of the current day had already passed. So learn from this that two days are needed besides the current day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains משה's reasoning. Each day of separation must be a full day with the night before it, and the day ה׳ spoke to him was already missing its night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ spoke to משה in the morning, so "today" no longer had its preceding night and could not count as a complete day. משה therefore counted two complete days after that one, which adds up to three days in total, matching רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Today is like tomorrow
Its night is together with it
Now; the current day
Learn from it; conclude from it
Besides; not counting

steps.confusionAlert: The night that counts here is the night BEFORE the day, as in the Jewish day. Since ה׳ spoke in the morning, that night was already gone.

phrases.english: "Today and tomorrow" — today is like tomorrow.
Just as tomorrow has its night with it,
so too today must have its night with it.
But the night of the present day had already passed,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי לְבַר מֵהָאִידָּנָא.
phrases.english: so learn from it: two days besides the present day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה compared "today" to "tomorrow": each needs its preceding night. Since today's night had passed, he required two full days after it.

steps.title: Proof ה׳ agreed: the שכינה came only on שבת morning
steps.stepSummary: We know ה׳ agreed with the added day because the שכינה did not rest on the mountain until שבת morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know ה׳ agreed with him? Because the שכינה did not rest on the mountain until שבת morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know ה׳ approved of משה's extra day. It answers that ה׳ waited until שבת morning, the date that fits משה's count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the plain command, the Torah could have been given a day earlier. Since the שכינה came only on שבת morning, ה׳ followed משה's extended schedule, which shows His agreement.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?
The Divine Presence rested
Shabbat morning

phrases.aramaic: וּמְנָלַן דְּהִסְכִּים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל יָדוֹ —
phrases.english: And from where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, agreed with him?

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא שְׁרַאי שְׁכִינָה עַד צַפְרָא דְשַׁבְּתָא.
phrases.english: Because the Divine Presence did not rest until Shabbat morning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָלַן דְּהִסְכִּים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל יָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second half of the ברייתא's claim (ה׳'s agreement) for the first item.
steps.raayaObject: ה׳ agreed with משה's added day
steps.raayaSupportSource: The timing of the revelation: the שכינה came only on שבת morning

steps.title: What was משה's reasoning for separating from his wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the second item of the ברייתא and asks what reasoning led משה to separate from his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he separated from his wife — what did he interpret?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second item on the ברייתא's list. It asks what led משה to separate permanently from his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as step 6: first the reasoning, then the proof that ה׳ agreed. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He separated

phrases.english: And he separated from his wife — what did he interpret?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second item of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind משה's permanent separation from his wife

steps.title: משה's קל וחומר from the people at Sinai
steps.stepSummary: משה reasoned with a קל וחומר: if the people had to separate before one scheduled meeting with the שכינה, then he, who is spoken to at any moment, must surely separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: He made a קל וחומר by himself and said: Israel, with whom the שכינה spoke only one time, and ה׳ set a time for them — still the Torah said "Be ready... do not approach a woman." I, with whom the שכינה speaks at every moment and no time is set for me, how much more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains משה's reasoning. He compared himself to the people at הר סיני and concluded that he must separate permanently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people had one prophecy at a known time, yet they still had to separate. משה receives prophecy all the time without warning, so he must always be ready, which means separating permanently.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
And He set a time for them
"And be prepared" (שמות יט:טו)
How much more so

phrases.english: He reasoned an a fortiori argument by himself, and said:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא דִּבְּרָה שְׁכִינָה עִמָּהֶן
phrases.english: If Israel, with whom the Divine Presence spoke

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שָׁעָה אַחַת, וְקָבַע לָהֶן זְמַן,
phrases.english: only one time, and He set a time for them,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה: ״וְהָיוּ נְכֹנִים וְגוֹ׳ אַל תִּגְּשׁוּ״.
phrases.english: the Torah said: "Be prepared... do not approach a woman."

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי, שֶׁכׇּל שָׁעָה וְשָׁעָה שְׁכִינָה מְדַבֶּרֶת עִמִּי,
phrases.english: I, with whom the Divine Presence speaks at every moment,
and He does not set a time for me,
all the more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה about משה's separation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the people at Sinai: one scheduled prophecy required separation, so constant unscheduled prophecy requires permanent separation.

steps.title: Proof ה׳ agreed: "Return to your tents" but "you stand here with Me"
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ told the people to return to their tents (their wives) but told משה to stay with Him. This shows ה׳ approved of משה's separation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know ה׳ agreed? As it is written: "Go tell them: Return to your tents", and right after it is written: "And you, stand here with Me."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that ה׳ agreed with משה's separation. The people were sent home to their wives, but משה was told to remain with ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Return to your tents" permitted the people to go back to family life after מתן תורה. The very next פסוק singles out משה to stay, which means he was not permitted to return, confirming his reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: "Return to your tents" — i.e., to your wives (דברים ה:כו)
"And you, stand here with Me" (דברים ה:כז)
And it is written after it

phrases.aramaic: וּמְנָלַן דְּהִסְכִּים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל יָדוֹ? —
phrases.english: And from where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, agreed with him?
As it is written: "Go say to them:
Return to your tents",
and it is written after it: "And you, stand here with Me."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָלַן דְּהִסְכִּים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל יָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves ה׳'s agreement with the second item.
steps.raayaObject: ה׳ agreed with משה's separation from his wife
steps.raayaSupportSource: The contrast between "שובו לכם לאהליכם" and "ואתה פה עמד עמדי"

steps.title: Another opinion: "Mouth to mouth I speak with him"
steps.stepSummary: Some say the proof of ה׳'s agreement is the פסוק "פה אל פה אדבר בו", where ה׳ defends משה's special status.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say the proof is: "Mouth to mouth I speak with him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second possible proof that ה׳ agreed with משה's separation. This one comes from ה׳'s rebuke of אהרן and מרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When אהרן and מרים criticized משה about his wife, ה׳ answered that He speaks with משה "mouth to mouth", unlike other נביאים. That answer defends משה's unique level of prophecy, which is exactly why he had to separate, so ה׳ endorsed his decision.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say
"Mouth to mouth I speak with him" (במדבר יב:ח)

steps.whatToRemember: For each thing משה did on his own, the גמרא gives two pieces: his reasoning (מאי דרש) and the proof ה׳ agreed (ומנלן דהסכים). For separating from his wife, the reasoning is a קל וחומר, and the proof is "ואתה פה עמד עמדי" or, according to some, "פה אל פה אדבר בו".

phrases.aramaic: וְאִית דְּאָמְרִי: ״פֶּה אֶל פֶּה אֲדַבֶּר בּוֹ״.
phrases.english: And some say: "Mouth to mouth I speak with him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative source for the same proof.
steps.raayaObject: ה׳ agreed with משה's separation from his wife
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר יב:ח‎ — ה׳'s defense of משה to אהרן and מרים

steps.title: What reasoning led משה to break the Tablets?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the third item of the ברייתא and asks what reasoning led משה to break the לוחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He broke the Tablets. What did he learn that led him to do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next thing משה did on his own: breaking the לוחות. It asks what reasoning he used, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking something written by ה׳ is drastic, so משה must have had a source or a logical argument. The question follows the same pattern used earlier for the extra day and for separating from his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tablets of the Covenant
What did he expound / what reasoning did he use?

phrases.english: He broke the Tablets,
what did he expound (to reach this)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the second item of the ברייתא (separating from his wife) to the third item (breaking the לוחות).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind משה's decision to break the לוחות.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: משה reasoned: if a מומר may not eat the קרבן פסח, which is only one מצוה, then a nation of מומרים surely may not receive the whole Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: The קרבן פסח is only one of the תרי״ג מצוות, and the תורה said, 'No estranged person shall eat of it.' Here the entire תורה is involved and the Jewish people are acting as מומרים. All the more so they may not receive it!
steps.whatsHappening: משה built a קל וחומר. A single מצוה, the קרבן פסח, is kept from a מומר, so the whole Torah should certainly not be handed to a people serving the עגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'בן נכר' is understood to include a Jew who has turned to idolatry. The 'light' case is one מצוה and the 'heavy' case is the entire Torah. That makes withholding the לוחות an even stronger requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: The 613 commandments
An estranged person (here including a Jew who has turned to idolatry)
Apostates
All the more so (the conclusion of a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: He said: Just as the Pesach offering,
which is one of the 613 מצוות,
the Torah said:
'And no estranged person shall eat of it.'
Here the entire Torah is involved,
and Israel are apostates (serving the Calf),
all the more so (they may not receive it).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: וּמָה פֶּסַח שֶׁהוּא אֶחָד מִתַּרְיָ״ג מִצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the קרבן פסח: one מצוה is withheld from מומרים, so the entire Torah surely is.

steps.title: ה׳ approved: 'יישר כחך ששברת'
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ approved of the breaking, as shown by the words 'אשר שברת,' which ריש לקיש reads as 'יישר כחך ששברת.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, agreed with him? As it says, 'which you broke,' and ריש לקיש said: [read it as] 'Well done that you broke them.'
steps.whatsHappening: Just as in steps 8 and 11, the גמרא shows that ה׳ agreed with what משה did. Here the proof is from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אשר' seems extra, so ריש לקיש reads it as a hint to 'יישר,' meaning 'well done.' ה׳ is praising משה for breaking the לוחות, not criticizing him.

keyTerms.meaning: Agreed / approved
'Which you broke' (שמות לד:א)
May your strength be firm, meaning 'well done'
The אמורא רבי שמעון בן לקיש

steps.whatToRemember: All three things משה did on his own (adding a day, separating from his wife, breaking the לוחות) were based on his own reasoning, and ה׳ approved each one.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that He agreed,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, with him?
As it says: 'which you broke,'
and Reish Lakish said:
Well done that you broke them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָלַן דְּהִסְכִּים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל יָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves that ה׳ approved of the reasoning in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: ה׳'s approval of משה breaking the לוחות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'אשר שברת' as explained by ריש לקיש.

steps.title: 'Be ready for the third day' challenges רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'והיו נכונים ליום השלישי' suggests a three-day count, which seems to fit the רבנן and not רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And be ready for the third day.' This is difficult for רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the dispute between רבי יוסי and the רבנן about the date of מתן תורה. It raises a פסוק that seems to contradict רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that the Torah was given on the 7th of סיון, after three days of separation. ה׳'s own words say 'the third day,' which implies only two days of separation. That matches the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source)
Ready / prepared
It is difficult

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'And be ready for the third day,'
this is difficult for Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the list of משה's actions and goes back to the date dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's view that the Torah was given on the 7th of סיון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ה׳ said 'the third day,' which implies the 6th, not the 7th.

steps.title: משה added a day on his own
steps.stepSummary: The answer: ה׳ did say 'the third day,' but משה added one day on his own, as already established.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we already said that משה added one day on his own initiative.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing back to what it taught earlier: משה added a day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק records ה׳'s original plan of 'the third day.' משה extended it by one day, and ה׳ agreed (step 8). So the Torah was actually given on the 7th, and רבי יוסי's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Added
On his own initiative / by his own reasoning

phrases.english: Didn't we say
that Moshe added one day on his own?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אָמְרִינַן יוֹם אֶחָד הוֹסִיף מֹשֶׁה מִדַּעְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the פסוק describes ה׳'s original plan, before משה added a day.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'The third day' is the actual day the Torah was given.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'The third day' was ה׳'s original plan. משה added one more day of separation, so the Torah was given a day later and רבי יוסי is not contradicted.

steps.title: 'Third of the month and third of the week' challenges the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the day was both the third of the month and the third of the week. That implies ראש חודש fell on Sunday, which contradicts the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Third' means the third of the month and the third of the week. This is difficult for the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: Now a challenge is raised against the other side, the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the third of the month was a Tuesday, then ראש חודש סיון was on Sunday. That is רבי יוסי's view. The רבנן hold that ראש חודש was on Monday, so this ברייתא seems to contradict them.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the month
Of the week
The Sages (the majority view)

phrases.english: Come and hear: 'Third' —
the third of the month and the third of the week,
this is difficult for the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״שְׁלִישִׁי״ — שְׁלִישִׁי בַּחֹדֶשׁ וּשְׁלִישִׁי בַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי יוסי, the גמרא now challenges the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's view that ראש חודש סיון was on Monday.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes the 3rd of the month a Tuesday, which places ראש חודש on Sunday.

steps.title: That ברייתא follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that this ברייתא reflects רבי יוסי's opinion, so it does not bind them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן can say to you: Whose view is this? It is רבי יוסי's.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered by assigning the ברייתא to the other opinion in the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A source that matches one side of a מחלוקת cannot be used to disprove the other side. The רבנן simply disagree with this ברייתא's assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
They can say to you

phrases.english: The Rabbis can say to you:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Yosei's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לָךְ רַבָּנַן: הָא מַנִּי — רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the source follows the opposing opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is a neutral fact that everyone accepts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, so the רבנן are not contradicted.
steps.whatToRemember: Each side of the date dispute survives its challenge. רבי יוסי explains 'the third day' as ה׳'s original plan, and the רבנן attribute the ברייתא to רבי יוסי.

steps.title: According to the רבנן, third to what?
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא's 'third of the month' is רבי יוסי's view, then what does 'the third day' mean according to the רבנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Third' — relative to what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the 'third' day of the ברייתא was, and what happened on it, according to the רבנן. This sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matched the third of the month to Tuesday, which is רבי יוסי's view. For the רבנן, ראש חודש was Monday, so the third of the month was Wednesday. The גמרא asks what happened on that day according to them. The answer, built up over the next three steps, is that it was the day of the מצוה of הגבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Relative to what? / for what?

phrases.english: 'Third' — relative to what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the רבנן's rejection of the ברייתא in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What took place on the 'third' day (the 3rd of the month) according to the רבנן.

steps.title: A ברייתא on two verses about משה reporting to ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The answer begins by quoting a ברייתא that points out two verses where משה brings the people's words back to ה׳. This shows there were two separate exchanges.
steps.simpleTranslation: As was taught: 'And משה brought back the words of the people to ה׳,' and it is written, 'And משה told the words of the people to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering by bringing a ברייתא. This step only quotes the two verses, setting up the explanation of what the second exchange was about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate reports mean two separate messages. The second message turns out to be the command of הגבלה. That is what happened on the third of the month, a Wednesday in the רבנן's timeline.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
And he brought back (reported)
And he told

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's full point is only clear in the next two steps. These verses alone do not answer the question yet. They set up the identification of the second exchange as הגבלה.

phrases.english: As was taught in a Baraita:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיָּשֶׁב מֹשֶׁה אֶת דִּבְרֵי הָעָם אֶל ה׳״,
phrases.english: 'And Moshe brought back the words of the people to ה׳,'

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וַיַּגֵּד מֹשֶׁה אֶת דִּבְרֵי הָעָם אֶל ה׳״.
phrases.english: and it is written: 'And Moshe told the words of the people to ה׳.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכִדְתַנְיָא: ״וַיָּשֶׁב מֹשֶׁה אֶת דִּבְרֵי הָעָם אֶל ה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא identifying the second exchange as the הגבלה command. According to the רבנן, that is what took place on the third of the month.

steps.title: What was said in the second exchange?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what the content of the second exchange was, since the פסוק does not say.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, say to משה, and what did משה say to Israel, and what did Israel say to משה, and what did משה report back before the Almighty?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, a question is asked: what message went back and forth here? This prepares the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second verse mentions משה reporting the people's words, but the Torah never spells out what new message was given. The ברייתא wants to fill in that missing message.

keyTerms.meaning: Replied / reported back
The Almighty (literally 'the Power')

phrases.aramaic: מָה אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה,
phrases.english: What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, say to Moshe,
and what did Moshe say to Israel,
and what did Israel say to Moshe,
and what did Moshe report back before the Almighty?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the content of the exchange implied by the verses in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The content of the message in the second exchange.

steps.title: It was the command of setting boundaries
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says the second exchange was the מצוה of הגבלה, setting boundaries around the mountain.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the מצוה of setting boundaries. These are the words of רבי יוסי בר יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the unnamed message was the command of הגבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the הגבלה was given on its own separate day. For the רבנן, that day was the third of the month (Wednesday), as in their timeline in step 2. So the third day was the day of הגבלה, and the ברייתא's 'third of the week' does not bind them.

keyTerms.meaning: The command to set boundaries around הר סיני
A תנא (different from רבי יוסי of the date dispute)

phrases.english: This is the מצוה of setting boundaries,
the words of Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ מִצְוַת הַגְבָּלָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22, and through it, step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second exchange was הגבלה, and for the רבנן this took place on the third of the month.
steps.whyThisMatters: It lets the רבנן accept that something significant happened on the third of the month (the הגבלה) while rejecting the claim that it was also the third day of the week.

steps.title: רבי: first punishment, then reward
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads the two verbs differently: 'וישב' means משה first explained the punishment, and 'ויגד' means he later explained the reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: At first he explained its punishment, as it says 'וישב' — words that break a person's mind. In the end he explained its reward, as it says 'ויגד' — words that draw a person's heart like אגדה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי offers a different explanation of the two verses. They are not about הגבלה but about how משה presented the Torah to the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'וישב' as related to 'משבבין,' meaning shattering or breaking the mind, which refers to the frightening punishment. He reads 'ויגד' as related to 'אגדה,' meaning words that attract the heart, which refers to the reward.

keyTerms.meaning: Its punishment
The giving of its reward
Break / shatter
Aggadic teaching that attracts the heart

phrases.english: Rebbi says:
At first he explained its punishment,
as it is written: 'And Moshe reported (Vayashev)' —
words that break a person's mind;
and in the end he explained its reward,
as it is written: 'And Moshe told (Vayaged)' —

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁמּוֹשְׁכִין לִבּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם כְּאַגָּדָה.
phrases.english: words that draw a person's heart like aggada.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative explanation of the two verses, instead of רבי יוסי בר יהודה's הגבלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה first explained the punishment and then the reward.

steps.title: Some say: first reward, then punishment
steps.stepSummary: Others reverse רבי's order: 'וישב' refers to reward, which settles the mind, and 'ויגד' refers to punishment, which is as bitter as wormwood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: At first he explained its reward, as it says 'וישב' — words that settle a person's mind. In the end he explained its punishment, as it says 'ויגד' — words as hard for a person as wormwood.
steps.whatsHappening: A second version reads the same two words in the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'וישב' is read as 'משיבין,' meaning restoring or calming the mind, which refers to the reward. 'ויגד' is read as 'גידין,' meaning bitter wormwood, which refers to the punishment. The order is reversed from רבי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (an alternative version)
Restore / calm
Wormwood (something bitter)

steps.whatToRemember: The two verses are explained three ways: as the command of הגבלה (רבי יוסי בר יהודה), as punishment then reward (רבי), or as reward then punishment (איכא דאמרי).

phrases.english: And some say:
At first he explained its reward,
as it is written: 'And Moshe reported (Vayashev)' —
words that settle a person's mind;
and in the end he explained its punishment,
as it is written: 'And Moshe told (Vayaged)' —
words that are as hard for a person as wormwood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: בַּתְּחִילָּה פֵּירֵשׁ מַתַּן שְׂכָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses רבי's order of punishment and reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה first explained the reward and then the punishment.

steps.title: A ברייתא calls the day 'sixth of the month and sixth of the week'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that describes a day as both the sixth of the month and the sixth of the week (Friday). This seems to clash with the רבנן's calendar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'The sixth' means the sixth of the month and the sixth of the week. This is difficult for the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא and uses it to challenge the רבנן's view of when the days at סיני fell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, ראש חודש סיון did not fall on Sunday. That means the sixth of the month could not also be Friday, the sixth of the week. Only with רבי יוסי's calendar, where ראש חודש fell on Sunday, do the two 'sixths' line up. So this ברייתא looks like a problem for the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. This introduces a source used as a proof or a challenge.
The sixth day of the month
The sixth day of the week (Friday)
It is difficult. This marks a challenge against a view.
The Sages, who argue with רבי יוסי here

steps.confusionAlert: 'שִׁשִּׁי בַּשַּׁבָּת' does not mean 'the sixth on שבת.' Here 'שבת' means the week, so the phrase means Friday.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'The sixth' means the sixth of the month,
and the sixth of the week,
This is difficult for the Rabbis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the calendar debate between רבי יוסי and the רבנן after the aside about וישב and ויגד.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's view of which weekday ראש חודש סיון fell on
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the sixth of the month was also the sixth of the week, ראש חודש must have been Sunday. That matches רבי יוסי, not the רבנן.

steps.title: This ברייתא also follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא, like the earlier one, was taught according to רבי יוסי. So it is no problem for the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא too is the view of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the רבנן by saying this ברייתא simply follows the other opinion, רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'also' (נָמֵי) shows that the גמרא has already used this same answer for an earlier source. A source that matches one side of a מחלוקת does not disprove the other side. The רבנן just disagree with this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: This, too. It points back to an earlier source answered the same way.
It follows רבי יוסי's view

phrases.english: This, too, is the view of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to the opposing תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was assumed to be accepted by everyone, so it would disprove the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי only, and the רבנן hold differently.

steps.title: According to the רבנן, what was that day 'the sixth' of?
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, the גמרא asks how the רבנן would explain the word 'sixth.' רבא begins to answer, and his answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The sixth' of what? רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן understand the word 'sixth.' This sets up רבא's answer, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'sixth' still has to mean something for the רבנן, but for them it cannot mean Friday the sixth of the month. So the גמרא looks for another way to count to six that would work for the רבנן. Only the opening words 'רבא said' appear here.

keyTerms.meaning: Of what? / With respect to what?
רבא said. This introduces the answer.

phrases.english: The sixth of what?
phrases.notes: That is, according to the Rabbis.

phrases.english: Rava said:
phrases.notes: The attribution opens רבא's answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After placing the ברייתא with רבי יוסי, the גמרא asks how the רבנן would read the word 'sixth.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'sixth' refers to according to the רבנן
